subject: PayWell integration: auth options, SDK handoff, and next steps
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@paywell.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: PayWell integration: auth options, SDK handoff, and next steps

Hi Sara —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Per our conversation, I put together a short follow-up covering the authentication options we discussed and suggested next steps for the SDK handoff and routing/structured-output concerns. Attached: a lightweight requirements sheet and a short note on auth trade-offs (PDF).

Quick summary of options we covered:
- Short-lived API keys via our SDK (easy dev onboarding, easier rotation via admin console)
- OAuth 2.0 client credentials / JWT service account (recommended for server-to-server with least-privilege tokens and central rotation via your KMS)
- Ephemeral tokens + mTLS (for stricter network controls — we can scope this to Dedicated/Private deployments)

Items I need from your side to finalize a mutual action plan:
1) Which environment do you plan to run inference from (paywell-prod in us-east-1 or on-prem)?
2) Who is your security lead (to loop in for the rotation schedule and evidence requirements)?
3) Any constraints on long-lived secrets (e.g., forbidden in S3, must be in HSM)?

Proposed near-term plan (if it works for you):
- This week: Team sync (30 min) to pick auth pattern and confirm network model.
- Next week: Redwood provides an SDK quickstart repo and sample service-account JWT flow (POC).
- Week +2: Joint test: token rotation exercise and embedding/reranker smoke test.

Ben and Marissa are copied for implementation details: Ben will own the SDK quickstart and Marissa will coordinate the integration playbook.

Regards,
Karthik
Director, Solutions 
Redwood Inference

Attachments: paywell_integration_requirements.xlsx, redwood-auth-options.pdf
From: Sara Liu <sara.liu@paywell.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@paywell.com>, security@paywell.com
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PayWell integration: auth options, SDK handoff, and next steps

Thanks Karthik — this is helpful. A couple of clarifying points from our side: 

- We prefer server-to-server JWT service accounts for core production (we have an internal KMS/HSM policy and want short-lived tokens minted by our auth server).
- For initial POC, we can run from paywell-stage (us-east-1) — prod onboarding is gated behind a security review.
- Our security lead is Alex Gomez (cc'd); he'll need the rotation cadence and evidence artefacts (SOC2-style artifacts are ideal).

Questions: 
1) Can Redwood's SDK support token refresh using our internal token-exchange endpoint (we'd like to avoid storing long-lived keys in the SDK config)?
2) For embeddings/reranker calls, is there a recommended pattern for per-tenant prefixes/caching to avoid cross-tenant leakage?

We can do a 30-minute tech sync Thu or Fri — Alex prefers Fri morning PT.

Sara Liu
VP, Product
PayWell
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@paywell.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@paywell.com>, security@paywell.com
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 14:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PayWell integration: auth options, SDK handoff, and next steps

Sara — great. Short answers inline and then a proposed MAP (mutual action plan).

Q1 — SDK + token-exchange: Yes. Our SDK supports pluggable credential providers; we have an example that calls an internal token-exchange endpoint to mint short-lived tokens (we never persist long-lived secrets in the client). For the POC we'll deliver a sample credential provider implementation that hits your exchange endpoint and swaps for a Redwood-access token.

Q2 — embeddings/reranker per-tenant isolation: Recommended pattern is:
- Per-tenant prefixing for cache keys + tenant-scoped KV namespaces for any prefix/KV caching.
- On the routing side, mark requests with tenant_id in header (we support X-Tenant-ID) and enforce strict cache key scoping in the SDK/runtime.

Proposed Mutual Action Plan (dates relative to this week):
- Thu 2027-04-29 09:30 PT: 30m tech sync (agenda: token-exchange flow, network egress, initial capacity for embeddings).
- By Mon 2027-05-03: Redwood delivers SDK quickstart repo, sample token-exchange provider, and an example embedding + reranker config. (artifact: github.com/redwood/paywell-poc)
- By Fri 2027-05-07: Joint POC run on paywell-stage with a rotation exercise (we will rotate a test service account and validate audit logs).

Attachments I flagged to you earlier include a brief note on evidence we can provide for rotation (audit log snippets, token issuance records) and a sample network diagram. See attached network_diagram.png.

Ben/Marissa — can you take the SDK quickstart and draft the initial README/tasks? Ben — add a short sample for the token-exchange provider (5–8 files). Marissa — create a one-pager runbook for the rotation test we can hand to PayWell security.

Thanks — looking forward to the sync.

Karthik

Quick note from the SDK side:
- I'll scaffold the quickstart with two credential providers: static-service-account (for lab) and token-exchange-provider (calls your exchange endpoint, caches token until expiry).
- For rotation exercise, the SDK will expose a rotate() API that our infra team can call; we'll include unit tests that simulate rotation and show audit log entries.
- Embeddings/reranker sample: default config will set a per-tenant cache TTL of 12h with explicit invalidation hooks — that'll avoid accidental mixing.

I'll attach the initial README to the repo and a sample curl showing the exchange flow.
